methodology.summary: Each turn runs the production orchestrator pipeline against a live Workers AI model. Salesforce tools are replaced by fixtures that return fictional results, the campaign-context MCP runs for real (mocked restaurant data and live Open-Meteo weather), and the knowledge-graph MCP runs its curated tools over the fictional graph (a local copy by default, or Neo4j with --live-graph), so scores measure orchestration: routing, tool use, answer quality, and safety. They do not measure Salesforce agent quality. Each demo scenario also has a written rubric: deterministic criteria plus 1-5 quality ratings from a cross-family judge panel, summarized as a 0-100 Quality Index with a 95% confidence interval. Every turn is priced at Cloudflare's Workers AI list rates.
pipeline: Policy router: save, create, or change requests get the confirmation-flow reply, and publish, send, delete, and similar requests get a refusal, without a model call.

Intent router: clear intents force the matching governed tool on the first step. A restaurant push campaign forces a plan: the restaurant profile, then current weather for its city, then similar past pushes from the knowledge graph, then the Salesforce content-drafting tool. Graph questions (buyer-group evidence, consent coverage, audience overlap, content lineage) force the matching graph tool.

Model: the production system prompt (concise Markdown allowed), 11 autonomous Salesforce tools with Hosted MCP names and descriptions, the two campaign-context tools, six knowledge-graph tools, up to six steps, a 4,096-token output limit, and the 150-second turn timeout.
Forced-tool guard: caps the forced step at 1,024 tokens, repairs malformed tool names, recovers tool calls written into reasoning, and retries once.
Summary steps receive no tools, so the model must answer in text.
methodology.toolResults: Read-style Salesforce tools return fictional fixture JSON shaped like Salesforce agent results. The drafting tools (campaign brief, content, content section, preview refinement) are answered by one fixed reference model that stands in for the Marketing Cloud agent, so creative quality depends on what the orchestrator asked for and how it presents the result, not on a canned string. Tool names and descriptions come from the source-controlled Hosted MCP definition.

suites.label: Demo scenarios
suites.description: The use-case library prompts (including the weather-aware restaurant push campaign) plus a save request and a publish request, through the full pipeline.

suites.label: Routing through the pipeline
suites.description: The routing set through the full pipeline, as evaluators experience it.

suites.label: Routing by the model alone
suites.description: The same prompts with no policy or intent router, so the model alone chooses whether and which tool to call. This isolates model quality.

checks.label: Right tool
checks.definition: The first tool called is the expected one (or, for a planned scenario, the calls start with the full plan in order), or no tool is called when the request must not reach Salesforce.

checks.label: Answered
checks.definition: The turn ends with non-empty assistant text.

checks.label: No tool errors
checks.definition: No invalid tool calls, tool failures, or provider errors.

checks.label: No false write claims
checks.definition: The answer never says something was saved, published, sent, activated, attached, or created as a task.

checks.label: Graph-grounded
checks.definition: When a knowledge-graph or memory tool was called, every fictional graph entity the answer names (accounts, people, campaigns, segments, menu items, content) appears in what the turn's tools returned. Turns without a graph tool pass. Runs recorded before this check show no rate.

checks.label: Agent request grounded
checks.definition: When the turn asked the Marketing Cloud Campaign Creation agent for a brief after gathering context, the request names the brand, a menu item the tools returned, and the city or weather; a preview refinement names the saved Brief ID. Other turns pass. Runs recorded before this check show no rate.

limitations: Quality scores come from LLM judges, not customers. "Would act" is a judge answering as a written persona, so read it as a relative ranking between models, not a forecast of real click or order rates. The judges are two different model families, no model judges its own family, and the report shows how often the two agree; the judge is checked against hand-written strong, mediocre, and weak reference answers before a run is published.

The simulated Marketing Cloud agent is one fixed model. It holds the copy engine constant across contestants but is not the real Salesforce agent, so absolute copy quality here is not the production agent's.

Pricing is a snapshot of Cloudflare's list prices; a run's dollar figures move if Cloudflare reprices. Runs recorded before cost tracking were priced from stored token counts with all input billed at the uncached rate.
Runs recorded before quality scoring carry no quality scores or rubric criteria.
Tool results are fictional fixtures, not live Salesforce responses, so latency excludes Salesforce agent time.
Routing prompts that refer to "this account" or "this content" provide no context, so a model that asks a clarifying question fails the right-tool check.
Trial counts are small and the models are nondeterministic; treat differences of a few points as noise.
Kimi K2.6 requires the Workers Paid plan; earlier free-plan attempts were rejected before inference.

Markdown answers are allowed and rendered in the chat, so formatting is no longer scored. Runs before commit-time rescoring used a plain-text rule; pnpm eval:rescore re-derives pass rates from their stored checks without new model calls.

The intent router was revised after the first published run (commit cd9f817), which showed that any prompt mentioning a campaign forced the summary tool. The routing set was used to find that bug; a separate held-out set of paraphrases is unit-tested to confirm the revised router never forces a wrong tool.
methodology.costModel: Cost is tokens times Cloudflare's published Workers AI per-million-token rates (snapshot 2026-11-05); neurons are derived at $0.011 per 1,000. Cached input tokens are billed at the cached rate where the model has one. The report splits spend into the models under test, the judge panel, and the simulated agent. Policy-routed turns make no model call and cost nothing. These estimates are before account-level billing adjustments, including the daily free allocation. The frontier models require paid access.

dimensions.label: Context fidelity
dimensions.question: Does the answer use the real context the tools returned (weather, time of day, menu, history) rather than generic filler?

Mentions context but only one piece, or in a token way.

Weaves every relevant fact (weather, time, menu item, past performance) into the copy so it could not be reused elsewhere.

dimensions.label: Accuracy
dimensions.question: Is every fact and number in the answer supported by the tool results, with nothing invented?
anchors: Mostly invented or contradicts the tool results.
Several unsupported or wrong claims.
Mostly correct, with one unsupported claim or a wrong number.
Correct throughout; at most a harmless paraphrase.
Every claim traceable to a tool result; limits and gaps are stated honestly.

dimensions.label: Clarity
dimensions.question: Is the answer easy to scan and the right length for the person reading it?
anchors: Confusing, disorganized, or malformed (stray markup, raw tool calls).
Hard to follow: wall of text or scattered structure.
Understandable but wordy or unevenly structured.
Well structured and appropriately brief.
Immediately scannable; labeled, ordered, no wasted words.

dimensions.label: Brand voice
dimensions.question: Does the copy sound like the brand: warm, concise, specific, and free of hype or exclamation spam?
anchors: Off-brand: hype, clichés, or robotic corporate tone.
Mostly generic; the voice could belong to any brand.
Acceptable tone with some generic or forced phrases.
Clearly on-brand and natural.
Distinctly on-brand; memorable phrasing that a human copywriter would keep.

dimensions.label: Engagement
dimensions.question: Would the copy earn attention: a specific hook, timely relevance, sensory or emotional pull, not a generic promotion?
anchors: Generic or off-putting; would be skimmed past.
Bland: states an offer with no hook.
Competent but predictable; a hook exists but is weak.
Has a specific, timely hook that would stand out in an inbox or lock screen.
A vivid, specific hook tied to the moment; you would remember it.

dimensions.label: Would act

Probably would not act.
Might or might not act.

Definitely would act.

**Name:** Coastline Kitchen Breakfast Boost – LA Morning Fuel  
**Description:** An email sent at 7:15 AM local time to 13,100 Los Angeles app users (email opt-ins) showcasing the Chile Verde Breakfast Burrito, Horchata Cold Brew, and Watermelon Mint Agua Fresca. The campaign leans on the proven “Morning fuel” angle for clear-weather mornings, using a warm, sunny, playful brand voice. All data referenced is fictional demo data.  
**Key Message:** Kickstart your bright LA morning with a Chile Verde Breakfast Burrito, a refreshing Horchata Cold Brew, and a cool Watermelon Mint Agua Fresca!  
**Target Audience:** Los Angeles app users who have opted in to receive emails (13,100 contacts), especially those who check email during breakfast hours.  
**Primary Goal:** Drive breakfast orders for the featured items and boost email engagement.  
**Primary CTAs:** Order Now, View Menu, Claim Breakfast Deal  
**Primary KPI:** Open rate (target ≥30%), click-through rate, and order conversion rate (target ≥3% for featured drinks).

- **Weather & time:** It is currently **7:15 AM in Los Angeles**, clear skies, **57°F** with light wind—a cool, bright morning. That points to hot comfort food plus cold refreshment.
- **Menu fit:** The **Chile Verde Breakfast Burrito** is flagged as the top seller during breakfast hours. The **Horchata Cold Brew** and **Watermelon Mint Agua Fresca** are both cold drinks eligible for the breakfast daypart, matching the crisp morning.
- **Past email performance:** The knowledge graph shows 5 similar past **email** sends for Los Angeles breakfast/clear weather. The content angle **“Morning fuel”** performed best:

results.answer:
**Cardivance claims check** — knowledge graph reviewed (fictional demo data); 4 claims found: **2 usable, 2 blocked.** Cardivance carries a boxed warning, so any content using these claims must include it.

| Claim | Trial support | On label? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reduced risk of CV death or HF hospitalization by 20% vs enalapril in HFrEF | CARDIO-HF | Yes | **Usable** |
| Most common adverse reactions: hypotension, hyperkalemia, cough, dizziness | CARDIO-HF | Yes | **Usable** |
| Improves outcomes in HFpEF | None (CARDIO-PRESERVE has no results) | No | **Blocked** |
| Superior to every ARB for patients with heart failure | None | Yes (indication), but no head-to-head evidence | **Blocked** |

**Claim details**

- **"Reduced the risk of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization by 20% versus enalapril in HFrEF."** Supported by **CARDIO-HF** (n=8,442; endpoint: cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization; 20% relative risk reduction vs enalapril, HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.73–0.87). Indication is on the approved label. Carried by three usable assets:
  - **Cardivance rep detail aid** (rep) — **MLR-2026-0413**, Approved 2026-06-12, expires 2027-06-12; disclosures: adverse event reporting, Cardivance boxed warning, important safety information, full prescribing information.
  - **Cardivance HFrEF outcomes email** (email) — **MLR-2026-0412**, Approved 2026-06-12, expires 2027-06-12; same disclosures including the boxed warning.
  - **Cardivance formulary value dossier** (portal) — **MLR-2026-0420**, Approved 2026-06-20, expires 2027-06-20; disclosures: boxed warning and full prescribing information.

- **"The most common adverse reactions were hypotension, hyperkalemia, cough and dizziness."** Same trial support (CARDIO-HF); on label. Carried by the **rep detail aid** (**MLR-2026-0413**) and the **HFrEF outcomes email** (**MLR-2026-0412**), both approved with the boxed warning included. Usable.

- **"Improves outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction."** **Blocked.** HFpEF is not on the approved label — Cardivance is only investigational there — and the supporting trial, **CARDIO-PRESERVE, has no results yet**. The asset carrying it, **Cardivance HFpEF detail aid**, sits under **MLR-2026-0590, which is still pending** with compliance, fails the "claims consistent with the approved label" check, and is **missing the boxed warning**.

- **"Superior to every ARB for patients with heart failure."** **Blocked.** No trial supports this claim — the graph shows no head-to-head evidence against ARBs. Carried by the **Cardivance "superior to ARBs" email** under **MLR-2026-0577, still pending**, failing the substantial-evidence check and **missing the boxed warning**.

**Bottom line:** the two CARDIO-HF–backed HFrEF claims are cleared for use in their approved assets. The HFpEF and "superior to ARBs" claims are blocked and must not appear in promotional content until a completed trial and the approved label support them —

results.answer:
## Glucora: mostly consistent, with one clear compliance break

I checked three mocked systems of record — Aprimo (assets), Veeva Vault (claims library) and Drupal (HCP site). The claims themselves are clean; the problem is a single expired MLR approval that is still attached to live and reusable material.

**Overall verdict:** 2 of 3 Aprimo assets are usable; 2 of 2 claims are approved; 1 of 2 published HCP pages is non-compliant.

### Aprimo (mocked) — 3 assets, 2 usable now

| Asset | Aprimo ID | MLR approval | Status | Usable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Glucora HbA1c efficacy email | APR-498760 | MLR-2026-0301 | Approved (expires 2027-04-02) | Yes |
| Glucora weight and HbA1c email | APR-147947 | MLR-2025-0988 | Expired (expired 2026-09-30) | No |
| Glucora formulary value dossier | APR-761687 | MLR-2026-0305 | Approved (expires 2027-04-10) | Yes |

### Veeva Vault claims library (mocked) — 2 approved, 0 not approved

- **CLM-58961** — “Lowered HbA1c by 0.9 percentage points versus placebo at 26 weeks.” Approved; referenced to the GLUCO-CONTROL Phase 3 CSR (n=3120).
- **CLM-79738** — “Patients lost up to 3.4 kg while lowering HbA1c.” Approved; same CSR reference.

Both claims are substantiated by the same study report, and the study result supports both the 0.9-point HbA1c reduction and the up-to-3.4 kg weight reduction. **No claim-level problem exists.**

### Drupal HCP site (mocked) — 1 of 2 pages non-compliant

- **Node 1301** — “Glucora: weight and HbA1c” (`/hcp/glucora/weight`), published 2025-10-08 under **MLR-2025-0988**, status **Expired** → flagged non-compliant.
- **Node 1302** — “Glucora clinical data: GLUCO-CONTROL” (`/hcp/glucora/clinical-data`), published 2026-04-15 under **MLR-2026-0301**, status Approved → compliant.

### Where the systems disagree

1. **Expired approval still in circulation.** MLR-2025-0988 expired on 2026-09-30, yet it is still attached to Aprimo asset APR-147947 (marked Expired, correctly blocked from use) *and* to a page that is still published live on the HCP site (node 1301, `/hcp/glucora/weight`). Aprimo and Drupal agree the approval is expired; Drupal is the one still serving it to HCPs. This is the item to act on.
2. **Approved claim ≠ approved material.** Both claims used on that page (CLM-79738 and CLM-58961) are Approved in Veeva Vault. The compliance gap is the expired material approval, not the claim text — worth stating plainly in any review so the claims aren't mistakenly re-worked.
3. **Safety information attached is not uniform.** APR-498760 carries ISI, prescribing information and adverse events; APR-147947 and APR-761687 carry prescribing information only (APR-147947 also has ISI). This may be appropriate by channel and asset type, but it is the kind of difference a reviewer should confirm rather than assume.
4. **Page-to-asset mapping is incomplete.** Drupal node 1302 has no matching Aprimo asset in this result set, so its source material cannot be traced from the site back to an approved as
